stories.title: Is it true that tariffs do not raise consumer prices?
alternates: 7 sources say tariffs do not raise consumer prices. Does it hold up?
What the research says about tariffs do not raise consumer prices
stories.question: Is it true that tariffs do not raise consumer prices?
stories.whyWatch: 7 sources across 13 channels repeat it, and the study that checked it points the other way. Anyone who has heard the claim gains from seeing it tested.
stories.tension: What gets repeated against what was measured. NY Fed tariff pass-through study (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein): The staff report estimates that about 26 percent of a tariff increase passes through to consumer goods prices within a year, 64 percent directly via imported goods and 36 percent via domestically produced goods, and concludes the 2025 tariffs had economically and statistically significant effects on consumer prices.
stories.evidenceNeeded: A measurement of whether tariffs do not raise consumer prices, on the population and under the conditions the claim describes.
evidenceAvailable: NY Fed tariff pass-through study (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein): wrong (0.85, direct)
stories.premise: 7 sources assert "Tariffs do not raise consumer prices". NY Fed tariff pass-through study (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein): The staff report estimates that about 26 percent of a tariff increase passes through to consumer goods prices within a year, 64 percent directly via imported goods and 36 percent via domestically produced goods, and concludes the 2025 tariffs had economically and statistically significant effects on consumer prices. The gap between what gets repeated and what the data shows is the story.

arc.hook: Open on the claim in the sources' own words.
arc.conflict: Then the study that checked it: NY Fed tariff pass-through study (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein): The staff report estimates that about 26 percent of a tariff increase passes through to consumer goods prices within a year, 64 percent directly via imported goods and 36 percent via domestically produced goods, and concludes the 2025 tariffs had economically and statistically significant effects on consumer prices.
arc.evidence: Walk through NY Fed tariff pass-through study (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein): what was measured, on whom, and the caveats.
arc.resolution: Say exactly what the evidence rules out and what it leaves open, including any narrower version that survives.
arc.takeaway: What a viewer should do differently now that the claim is not what it seemed.
